source_text: Sed de illis ego virtutibus dico, quas usu iam perfectae rationis adipiscimur. Ac per hoc, quia id etiam hic sicut frequenter inculcari nobis fuit necesse, ad ea, quae inferimus, ut sit attentus lector, admoneo; videbit enim ita in nullo Traducianos differre a Manichaeis, ut non alia nobis obiciant argumentorum vice, quam quae in illorum libris tenentur. Feci id quidem etiam in primi operis mei libro quarto.
pass_a_gloss: But I speak of those virtues which we obtain by the use already of perfect reason. And through this, because it was necessary for us that this also here as frequently be impressed, I warn that the reader be attentive to those things which we bring in; for he will see that in nothing the advocates of inherited sin differ from the Manichaeans, so that they object to us in the place of arguments nothing other than what is held in their books. I have done this indeed also in the fourth book of my first work.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: But I am speaking of the virtues we acquire through the use of fully developed reason. Since it was necessary to stress this here, as often elsewhere, I now urge the reader to attend to what follows. The reader will see that advocates of inherited sin differ from Manichaeans in nothing, offering against us as arguments only what is contained in their books. I already demonstrated this in the fourth book of my first work.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
